summary: iter66 multi-format file bundles — backend 23/23 pytest PASS + frontend verified. Upload accepts 1–10 files (primary + variants), rejects 0 / 11 / duplicate-format at both layers. New formats dwg/jpg/png/webp/gcode/nc/tap all accepted (+ legacy STL/PDF/ZIP/SVG regression clean). Auto-thumbnail: jpg in bundle auto-fills thumbnail_url when user didn't supply one; explicit wins over auto. /variants POST (uploader-only, 409 on dup, 403 cross-user) and DELETE /{fmt} (400 primary, 404 unknown, persistence confirmed via GET). Frontend: file input has multiple + accept=.dxf,.dwg,.svg,.stl,.glb,.gltf,.ai,.eps,.pdf,.zip,.jpg,.jpeg,.png,.webp,.gcode,.nc,.tap; 11-file and duplicate-format rejected with inline error; FileCard bundle chips (◆PRIMARY orange + grey variant chips) render correctly (screenshot-confirmed on a just-uploaded DXF+JPG bundle).
critical_code_review_comments: community.py upload_design_file_direct: role==maker uses claims.sub as user_key (= maker slug) — consistent with maker_auth, fine. Buyer flow uses community_users.user_id — also fine.
Auto-thumbnail loop on line ~380: walks the full `uploaded` list (including primary). Works as specified — promotes the first jpg/png/webp whether it's the primary or a variant.

/variants POST (lines 406-462) and DELETE /variants/{fmt} (lines 465-492) check `role != 'maker' and uploader_id != sub` — this means ANY maker (even someone else's maker slug) can edit someone else's bundle. That's documented as 'for moderation' in the docstring, but worth flagging: it's effectively an ambient-admin privilege for every maker. If unintended, tighten to `slug != doc.maker_slug`.
r2_storage.py line 215-217: `.nc` and `.tap` map to text/x-gcode — semantically correct (CNC g-code dialects).
CommunityPage.jsx line 432-441: client-side dedupe matches backend — good symmetry. The inferFmt() GLTF→GLB + JPEG→JPG normalisation keeps the UI label consistent with what the server stores.
FileCard.jsx download dropdown (line 767-793): closes only via toggle click; no outside-click handler — once opened it stays until user clicks the Download button again. Minor UX polish candidate.
